propositions: test_perf asserts a fixed 50ms wall-clock budget on a single run of rebar.llm.overlap.retrieve() over 300 digests, causing flaky failures under CI runner contention.
The function's true cost is ~1.6ms median (measured locally with ~30x margin to budget), but CI samples inflate to ~180x the true cost due to transient runner CPU scheduling contention.

Single-sample wall-clock measurement is not robust to shared-runner CPU scheduling; best-of-N (minimum elapsed across >=5 runs) would allow at least one sample to hit a quiet scheduler slice and accurately reflect uncontended compute cost.

A real algorithmic regression would uniformly slow all N runs including the minimum, so changing to best-of-N measurement retains the guardrail's ability to catch regressions while eliminating false failures from transient contention.
